findings.title: Delivery-only recovery bypasses finalizeRebriefRequest, so flipJobToWorking is skipped
findings.detail: This branch hand-rolls delivery recording instead of calling finalizeRebriefRequest, so it skips flipJobToWorking. The crash window it targets (between the rebrief-event append and the status flip) leaves the lane in-review/delivered after its settled re-brief turn.
findings.recommended_fix: Route the delivery-only case through finalizeRebriefRequest (or call flipJobToWorking) so both recovery paths record identically and the lane returns to working as the live endpoint does.

findings.title: Rebrief endpoint keeps durable markers after a synchronous worker failure
findings.evidence: const markers = options.ledger.beginPendingRebrief({ jobId, note, briefing: job.briefing });
findings.detail: Markers are written before the try, but cleanup only deletes the AbortController: if rebriefFreshMinion rejects (no lane, spawn or prompt failure), markers are never cleared or escalated, so a later boot re-runs a rebrief the caller saw fail.
findings.recommended_fix: Catch rebriefFreshMinion failures in the handler: clear the markers when no worker turn started (or escalate immediately), keeping them only for failures that leave a resumable session.

findings.title: resolveResumeFile comment promises the latest minion but .find takes the first listAgents() match
findings.detail: The comment promises the job's latest minion, but .find returns the first match in listAgents() order; if that order is oldest-first, recovery resumes a stale worker's session instead of the interrupted re-brief worker's.
findings.recommended_fix: Select the newest minion deterministically (e.g., order agents by registration time descending) instead of relying on listAgents() order, or fix the comment if the order is actually newest-first.
